invariants.description: The report never presents a heuristic verdict as an LLM review, and a failed LLM call is recorded with its reason.
invariants.rationale: A timed-out LLM call used to be reported as 'LLM GATE APPROVAL 10/10'.

invariants.description: Scoring and the LLM prompt stay honest: no bonus for deleting code, no claim that a test suite ran, no instruction to approve deletions.
invariants.rationale: A -1982 line diff earned +0.5 and the LLM was told 'tests passed, approve with confidence'.

invariants.description: Large diffs are reviewed in parts, never silently truncated.
invariants.rationale: Only the first 80k characters used to reach the LLM.

invariants.description: Scope is only what the prompt or --scope declares: dirty files are never added to it, and a restart inherits baseline and scope instead of redefining them.
invariants.rationale: pre merged every dirty file into scope, and could be re-run after editing to widen it.

invariants.description: Post audits against the base commit recorded at pre, with raw porcelain -z paths.
invariants.rationale: Mid-task commits, renames and paths with spaces or Vietnamese characters used to escape the audit.

invariants.description: An invariant without an applicable check is UNVERIFIED, never counted as passed, and no fixed confidence is invented.
invariants.rationale: Irrelevant template invariants used to be marked 'Maintained' with a hardcoded 0.92 confidence.

invariants.description: SEC-003 cannot be silenced by a comment that mentions 'sanitize'.
invariants.rationale: Any innerHTML line containing the word 'sanitize' used to be skipped.

invariants.description: Git hooks never break unrelated commits: UTF-8 console, LF scripts, repo-local hooks chained via --git-common-dir.
invariants.rationale: A cp1252 crash in the global hook blocked every commit on the machine.

invariants.description: An approved session covers only the exact file contents it approved.
invariants.rationale: One old approval let an unrelated 19-file commit through unchecked.

checks.forbid: last guard session was approved, skipping

invariants.description: The rulebook cannot be weakened silently, and learned rules are written only after they pass on the current code.
invariants.rationale: Guard now writes LLM-discovered rules into guard.invariants.json; without these checks an agent could delete a failing rule to pass the gate.

invariants.description: Every version bump updates pyproject.toml, guard/__init__.py and docs/index.html (badge and footer) together.
invariants.rationale: Discovered by the LLM gate review

invariants.description: The INVARIANTS proposal prompt must require descriptions in the same language as the existing invariant descriptions with file paths wrapped in backticks
invariants.rationale: Discovered by the LLM gate review

checks.require: same language as the existing invariant descriptions

invariants.description: The repository domain is scored from several signals, never taken from the first marker file, and the build command is resolved per ecosystem.
invariants.rationale: First-match detection called Node backends frontend (package.json) and a fullstack app infra (Dockerfile), which also ran `docker build` as the build check.

invariants.description: Refresh rewrites only guard-owned content: directive blocks between guard markers and marked hook blocks; unmarked guard text is reported, not rewritten.
invariants.rationale: Guard now edits agent docs and repository hooks after upgrades; touching user content would be destructive.

checks.require: if DIRECTIVE_START not in text or DIRECTIVE_END not in text:
return None  # guard is referenced in some other form

invariants.description: An empty `guard.invariants.json` (e.g. just created by lazy setup) falls back to the domain template invariants instead of yielding none
invariants.rationale: Discovered by the LLM gate review

invariants.description: After a successful self-upgrade, the newly installed binary re-execs to run `hook refresh` instead of relying on the old in-process code
invariants.rationale: Discovered by the LLM gate review

invariants.description: A repository first visited by a newer guard gets its old hook and directive blocks refreshed during initial setup
invariants.rationale: Discovered by the LLM gate review

invariants.description: Global install writes only into agents installed on this machine and uninstall removes only the marked guard block, keeping the user's content and a foreign core.hooksPath.
invariants.rationale: guard install edits the user's global agent instruction files such as ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md.

invariants.description: Global install and uninstall touch only the global instruction files of agents whose config directory exists on this machine
invariants.rationale: Discovered by the LLM gate review

invariants.description: Users of older installations are told what is missing and how to fix it: guard doctor, `guard hook refresh` (run by update self) and the first command of a new version print the setup check with a fix command.
invariants.rationale: Upgrading only refreshes what guard wrote before; gaps such as missing directives or unmarked sections need a visible instruction.

invariants.description: Uninstall paths clear guard's recorded-repository registry so a later upgrade refresh cannot reinstall hooks into forgotten repositories
invariants.rationale: Discovered by the LLM gate review

invariants.description: Every row reported by `setup_health()` at level missing or warn carries the exact command that fixes it
invariants.rationale: Discovered by the LLM gate review

invariants.description: Guard never creates a diff in a user's repository: it writes only inside .git and the Git-excluded .guard/ folder, keeps .guard/ out of Git through info/exclude (never .gitignore), and learned or auto-created invariants go to the local file.
invariants.rationale: Guard edited repository agent docs, tracked hooks and guard.invariants.json, which users then had to explain in review.
